extracted.intended_audience: authors, reviewers and editors of health-research manuscripts (particularly submissions to the journal Brain Impairment)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and checklists for preparing and critically appraising reports of observational studies, diagnostic accuracy studies, and qualitative research in health/clinical contexts; intended to help authors address required items and reviewers/editors assess manuscript quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 1: Indicate study design in title or abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate the study’s design with a commonly used term in the title or the abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of STROBE 22‑item checklist addressing title and abstract; helps readers immediately recognise design (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional).

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 1b: Informative, balanced abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide in the abstract an informative and balanced summary of what was done and what was found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure abstract contains clear summary of methods and key results; supports indexing and rapid appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 2: Background and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the scientific background and rationale for the investigation being reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place study question in scientific context so readers understand why study was done.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 3: Objectives and hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: State specific objectives, including any prespecified hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear statement of aims and prespecified hypotheses to frame methods and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 4: Present key elements of study design early
rubrics_metrics.description: Present key elements of study design early in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce design features (e.g., cohort, case-control, cross-sectional) early so readers understand approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 5: Setting and dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the setting, locations, and relevant dates, including periods of recruitment, exposure, follow-up, and data collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide context for generalisability and timing; includes recruitment and data collection periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 6a: Participants — cohort eligibility and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohort study — Give the eligibility criteria, and the sources and methods of selection of participants. Describe methods of follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail inclusion/exclusion, recruitment sources and follow-up procedures for cohort studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 6a (case-control): Participants — case-control eligibility and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Case-control study — Give the eligibility criteria, and the sources and methods of case ascertainment and control selection. Give the rationale for the choice of cases and controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how cases and controls were identified and why those choices were appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 6a (cross-sectional): Participants — cross-sectional eligibility and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-sectional study — Give the eligibility criteria, and the sources and methods of selection of participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe sampling and inclusion for cross-sectional analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 6b: Matching details for matched studies
rubrics_metrics.description: For matched studies, give matching criteria and number of exposed and unexposed (cohort) or number of controls per case (case-control).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report matching factors and group sizes to allow assessment of matching effectiveness and confounding control.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 7: Definitions of variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly define all outcomes, exposures, predictors, potential confounders, and effect modifiers. Give diagnostic criteria, if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit definitions enable reproducibility and clarity in interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 8: Data sources and measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: For each variable of interest, give sources of data and details of methods of assessment (measurement). Describe comparability of assessment methods if there is more than one group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe measurement instruments, procedures, and comparability across groups to support validity assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 9: Bias — efforts to address potential sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any efforts to address potential sources of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report methods to reduce selection, information, and other biases (e.g., blinding, analytic strategies).

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 10: Study size/sample size rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the study size was arrived at.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sample size calculations or rationale for chosen sample to assess statistical power and precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 11: Quantitative variables handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how quantitative variables were handled in the analyses. If applicable, describe which groupings were chosen and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report transformations, categorisations and reasons to enable evaluation of analytic choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 12a: Statistical methods — confounding control
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe all statistical methods, including those used to control for confounding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify modelling approaches, adjustment variables, and rationale for confounder selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 12b: Statistical methods — subgroups and interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any methods used to examine subgroups and interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specify subgroup analyses and interaction tests; report methods to avoid data dredging.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 12c: Statistical methods — missing data
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how missing data were addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe imputation, complete-case analysis, sensitivity analyses and assumptions about missingness.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 12d: Statistical methods — design-specific analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohort study — If applicable, explain how loss to follow-up was addressed. Case-control study — If applicable, explain how matching of cases and controls was addressed. Cross-sectional study — If applicable, describe analytical methods taking account of sampling strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report design-tailored analytic considerations (e.g., weighting, clustering, matched analyses).

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 12e: Statistical methods — sensitivity analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any sensitivity analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report analyses that test robustness of primary findings to assumptions and analytic choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 13a: Results — participant flow and numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Report numbers of individuals at each stage of study — e.g., numbers potentially eligible, examined for eligibility, confirmed eligible, included in the study, completing follow-up, and analysed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider presenting a flow diagram to summarise stages and losses.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 13b: Results — reasons for nonparticipation
rubrics_metrics.description: Give reasons for nonparticipation at each stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report exclusions and reasons to assess selection bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 13c: Results — consider flow diagram
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider use of a flow diagram.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual depiction aids transparency of participant selection and attrition.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 14a: Descriptive data — participant characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Give characteristics of study participants (e.g., demographic, clinical, social) and information on exposures and potential confounders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide baseline tables and relevant descriptive statistics to contextualise analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 14b: Descriptive data — missing data per variable
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate number of participants with missing data for each variable of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency about missingness informs bias and precision assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 14c: Descriptive data — cohort follow-up time
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohort study — Summarise follow-up time (e.g., average and total amount).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report person-time or average follow-up to allow incidence/ rate calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 15: Outcome data — report events or summary measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohort study — Report numbers of outcome events or summary measures over time. Case-control study — Report numbers in each exposure category, or summary measures of exposure. Cross-sectional study — Report numbers of outcome events or summary measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present outcome data appropriate to design to support effect estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 16a: Main results — unadjusted and adjusted estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Give unadjusted estimates and, if applicable, confounder-adjusted estimates and their precision (e.g., 95% confidence interval). Make clear which confounders were adjusted for and why they were included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both crude and adjusted results with CIs and rationale for adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 16b: Main results — category boundaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Report category boundaries when continuous variables were categorised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State cut-points and rationale to allow understanding of categorisation effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 16c: Main results — translate relative to absolute risks
rubrics_metrics.description: If relevant, consider translating estimates of relative risk into absolute risk for a meaningful time period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide absolute measures for clinical interpretability where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 17: Other analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Report other analyses done — e.g., analyses of subgroups and interactions, and sensitivity analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly label post-hoc vs prespecified secondary analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 18: Discussion — key results summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarise key results with reference to study objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie main findings back to prespecified aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 19: Discussion — limitations, bias and imprecision
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss limitations of the study, taking into account sources of potential bias or imprecision. Discuss both direction and magnitude of any potential bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about likely biases and their possible effects on conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 20: Discussion — cautious overall interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Give a cautious overall interpretation of results considering objectives, limitations, multiplicity of analyses, results from similar studies, and other relevant evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overstating findings; situate within broader evidence and analytic constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 21: Discussion — generalisability
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the generalisability (external validity) of the study results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address applicability to other settings, populations, and time periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE Item 22: Other information — funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Give the source of funding and the role of the funders for the present study and, if applicable, for the original study on which the present article is based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare funding and funder role to allow appraisal of potential conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD Item 1: Identify diagnostic accuracy study
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the article as a study of diagnostic accuracy (recommend MESH heading 'sensitivity and specificity').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labeling facilitates indexing and retrieval of diagnostic accuracy studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD Item 2: State research questions/aims
rubrics_metrics.description: State the research questions or study aims, such as estimating diagnostic accuracy or comparing accuracy between tests or across participant groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify whether primary aim is estimation, comparison, subgroup evaluation, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD Item 3: Study population — inclusion/exclusion and setting
rubrics_metrics.description: The study population: The inclusion and exclusion criteria, setting and locations where the data were collected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe spectrum of disease and non-disease states to assess applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD Item 4: Participant recruitment basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Participant recruitment: Was recruitment based on presenting symptoms, results from previous tests, or the fact that the participants had received the index tests or the reference standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report recruitment mechanism to judge selection bias and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD Item 5: Participant sampling — consecutive series
rubrics_metrics.description: Participant sampling: Was the study population a consecutive series of participants defined by the selection criteria in items 3 and 4? If not specify how the participants were further selected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consecutive series increases representativeness; deviations should be explained.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD Item 6: Data collection timing (prospective/retrospective)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data collection: Was data collection planned before the index test and reference standard were performed (prospective study) or after (retrospective study)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective designs reduce bias from differential data availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD Item 7: Reference standard and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference standard and its rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define gold-standard and justify choice; affects estimates of accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD Item 8: Technical specifications of tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical specifications of material and methods involved including how and when measurements were taken, and/or cite references for index tests and reference standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient detail to reproduce testing procedures and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD Item 9: Definition and rationale for cutoffs/categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of and rationale for the units, cutoffs and/or categories of the results of the index tests and the reference standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-specify thresholds and rationale to avoid data-driven cutoff selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD Item 10: Training and expertise of test readers
rubrics_metrics.description: The number training and expertise of the persons executing and reading the index tests and the reference standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report reader experience to appraise generalisability and variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD Item 11: Blinding of readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether or not the readers of the index test and reference standard were blind (masked) to the results of the other test and describe any other clinical information available to the readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blinding reduces review bias; specify additional information available to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD Item 12: Statistical methods for diagnostic accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods for calculating or comparing diagnostic accuracy, and the statistical methods used to quantify uncertainty (e.g., 95% confidence intervals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe analytic techniques for sensitivity/specificity, ROC, predictive values, likelihood ratios, etc., and how uncertainty is quantified.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD Item 13: Methods for calculating reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods for calculating test reproducibility, if done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report intraclass correlations, kappa, Bland-Altman, or other reproducibility metrics when assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD Item 14: Dates of study and recruitment
rubrics_metrics.description: When study was done, including beginning and ending dates of recruitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dates contextualise technology, prevalence and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD Item 15: Clinical and demographic characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical and demographic characteristics of the study population (e.g., age, sex, spectrum of presenting symptoms, comorbidity, current treatments, recruitment centres).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide details necessary for judging spectrum bias and external validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD Item 16: Numbers undergoing tests and reasons for missing tests
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of participants satisfying the criteria for inclusion that did or did not undergo the index tests and/or the reference standard; describe why participants failed to receive either test (a flow diagram is strongly recommended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flow diagram recommended to show test execution order and exclusions; report reasons for missing tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD Item 17: Time interval and intervening treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Time interval from the index tests to the reference standard, and any treatment administered between.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delays or interventions between tests can change disease status and bias accuracy estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD Item 18: Disease severity distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of severity of disease (define criteria) in those with the target condition; other diagnoses in participants without the target condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report disease spectrum to evaluate performance across severity levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD Item 19: Cross-tabulation of index by reference results
rubrics_metrics.description: A cross-tabulation of the results of the index tests (including indeterminate and missing results) by the results of the reference standard; for continuous results, the distribution of the test results by the results of the reference standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide contingency tables to allow calculation of accuracy measures and transparency around indeterminate results.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD Item 20: Adverse events
rubrics_metrics.description: Any adverse events from performing the index tests or the reference standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report harms to balance benefit-risk considerations of implementing the test.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD Item 21: Estimates of diagnostic accuracy and uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimates of diagnostic accuracy and measures of statistical uncertainty (e.g. 95% confidence intervals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, likelihood ratios, AUC etc., with CIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD Item 22: Handling indeterminate, missing, outlier results
rubrics_metrics.description: How indeterminate results, missing responses and outliers of the index tests were handled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe rules for classifying indeterminate results and analytic approaches to missing/outliers.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD Item 23: Estimates of variability across subgroups/readers/centres
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimates of variability of diagnostic accuracy between subgroups of participants, readers or centres, if done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report heterogeneity to inform transportability and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD Item 24: Estimates of test reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimates of test reproducibility, if done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide repeatability/inter-rater reliability metrics where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD Item 25: Discussion — clinical applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the clinical applicability of the study findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret accuracy in terms of patient care decisions and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD: Use of a prototypical flow diagram
rubrics_metrics.description: A prototypical flowchart was developed to present detailed information about the method of patient recruitment, the order of test execution and the number of patients present and classified at each stage of a diagnostic accuracy study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flow diagram strongly recommended to transparently show recruitment, testing sequence, and participant counts at each stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Downs & Black scale: Method quality rating scale
rubrics_metrics.description: A method quality rating scale for observational studies (cohort and case-control) and randomised trials containing 26 items in four subscales: Reporting (10 items), Confounding (6 items), Bias (7 items) and External validity (3 items).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses both internal and external validity; reported inter-rater reliability moderate for total (r = .75); administration time averages 20–25 minutes (range 10–45 mins).

rubrics_metrics.name: QUADAS checklist: Quality assessment for diagnostic accuracy studies
rubrics_metrics.description: The QUADAS tool defines quality in terms of internal and external validity and contains 14 items covering bias (9 items), variability (2 items) and reporting (3 items).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developed systematically and evaluated empirically; used to assess methodological quality of diagnostic accuracy studies; some items were modified after evaluation (items on uninterpretable results and withdrawals).

rubrics_metrics.name: QUADAS (Cochrane 11-item) version
rubrics_metrics.description: An 11‑item version of QUADAS is recommended for quality assessment of studies in Cochrane Systematic Reviews of Diagnostic Accuracy (this version does not include the 3 reporting items from the original QUADAS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shorter Cochrane-adapted checklist used in systematic reviews; retains items relevant to bias and variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment note: Reproducibility of STARD and QUADAS assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproducibility studies show overall high agreement for STARD (inter-assessment agreement 85%; ICC = 0.79) and good agreement for QUADAS (85%–91% agreement with reviewers' consensus ratings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where disagreements occur, they often reflect poor reporting in articles rather than ambiguity of the checklist items themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Malterud guidance for qualitative research (30 items)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 30‑item guideline to guide review of qualitative manuscripts covering: aim (3 items), reflexivity (1 item), method and design (2 items), data collection and sampling (5 items), theoretical framework (3 items), analysis (4 items), findings (4 items), discussion (5 items), presentation (2 items), and references (1 item).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies across qualitative traditions; reproduced on the Qualitative Research Guidelines Project website; intended to guide reporting and appraisal of qualitative studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: RATS guideline (Clark): Relevance, Appropriateness, Transparency, Soundness (22 items)
rubrics_metrics.description: The RATS guideline lists 22 items across core areas: relevance of study question (2 items), appropriateness of qualitative method (1 item), sampling (2 items), recruitment (2 items), data collection (3 items), role of researchers (1 item), ethics (3 items), analysis (4 items), and discussion and presentation (4 items).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides additional methodological detail useful for less experienced authors/reviewers; available via EQUATOR network.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spencer et al. framework: Elemental quality appraisal (18 questions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Framework of 18 appraisal questions relevant across qualitative methods covering findings (5 questions), design (1), sample (2), data collection (1), analysis (4), reporting (2), reflexivity and neutrality (1), ethics (1), and auditability (1). Each question includes quality indicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elemental approach recognises methodological diversity across qualitative research; framework downloadable from UK Government Social Research Service website.

rubrics_metrics.name: JBI-QARI critical appraisal instrument (qualitative)
rubrics_metrics.description: JBI-QARI consists of 10 items focusing on philosophical and methodological congruity (5 items), explication of researcher biases (2 items), and representation of the participants’ perspectives and their relationship to the conclusions (3 items).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implemented in Joanna Briggs Institute software to support systematic review workflows (data extraction, synthesis), facilitating inclusion of qualitative findings in evidence synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on applicability of reporting guidelines to case reports/series
rubrics_metrics.description: Although STROBE was not developed for case reports or case series, authors/reviewers of case reports and case series may find a number of STROBE items applicable and the statement helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may selectively apply relevant checklist items to other study formats when helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial policy: Brain Impairment endorsement of reporting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Brain Impairment endorses commonly used reporting guidelines (STROBE, STARD, QUADAS, qualitative guidelines) and reviewers and editors will use these standards when assessing submissions to the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are strongly encouraged to adhere to relevant reporting guideline items when preparing manuscripts submitted to Brain Impairment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial requirement: Ethics approval statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Brain Impairment requires that authors include a statement about ethics approval to conduct their study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when checklists do not include ethics approval, the journal requires explicit ethics statements for research involving human participants (and animals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial guidance: Flexible formatting of checklist items
rubrics_metrics.description: Checklist items should be addressed in sufficient detail and with clarity somewhere in an article, but the order and format for presenting information depends on author preferences, journal style, and the traditions of the research field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use checklists to ensure content coverage rather than rigidly imposing the checklist order/format on manuscript structure (quotation from von Elm et al., 2007).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting guidelines are evolving documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting guidelines are recognised by their developers to be evolving documents, and they require revisions and refinement in the light of new information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult current versions and resources such as the EQUATOR Network library for updates and additional reporting guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource pointer: EQUATOR Network library
rubrics_metrics.description: The EQUATOR Network library is a useful resource including a library of health-research reporting guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to EQUATOR (http://www.equator-network.org/resource-centre/library-of-health-research-reporting/) for additional and updated reporting guidelines.
